topic: Choosing evidence for a final review
stem: Talia, a collegiate fencer, asked an online consultant for help with one thing: how nervous she feels in the minute before a bout. They agreed to judge progress on that. She completed the Test of Performance Strategies at intake and has sent a 1-to-10 nerves rating from the strip before every bout since. Her last bout of the season was Saturday, and their closing review is tomorrow. Which evidence should the consultant rely on most to judge progress?
options: Her TOPS scores from intake and from a new administration tomorrow
Her pre-bout ratings from early in the season and from recent bouts
Her scores on the CSAI-2, completed as tomorrow's review begins
Her coach's account of how composed she has looked before bouts
rationales: Repeating the TOPS fits a goal about how often she uses mental skills. Her agreed goal was how nervous she feels, which the TOPS doesn't measure.
Evaluation should use the measure that matches the agreed goal, gathered the same way over time. Her ratings capture felt nerves in the moment that matters, with early and recent points to compare.
The CSAI-2 would fit if she could complete it shortly before a bout. State anxiety at a review meeting says little about how she feels on the strip, and there is no earlier score to compare.
A coach's view helps when the goal is visible behavior. How nervous she feels is a private experience that outward composure can hide.
takeaway: Judge progress with the measure that matches the agreed goal and was gathered the same way throughout.

topic: Matching evaluation level to a decision
stem: An esports organization's consultant finished a two-day workshop on a new in-match call system yesterday. The five players now leave for a three-week break, with no scrims or matches until the day before their season opener. The general manager must decide today whether to pay for a refresher session on the final day of the break. He says it depends on whether players know which call to make in which situation. Which evaluation step best informs his decision?
options: Ratings from each player of how useful and engaging the workshop was
A scenario quiz asking each player which call fits each situation
Coding of the team's voice comms for use of the new calls in matches
The team's match results from before and after the workshop
rationales: Ratings show Kirkpatrick's reaction level. They would fit a decision about whether players value the workshop, not whether they know the calls.
The decision turns on knowledge, Kirkpatrick's learning level, and the players can be tested now. A scenario quiz shows directly whether each knows which call fits.
Coding comms addresses the behavior level and would be the choice if the question were whether players use the calls in competition. There are no matches to code before the decision.
Results address the fourth level. They come too late for this decision and depend on much more than knowing the calls.
takeaway: Choose the Kirkpatrick level that answers the decision at hand and can be measured in time.

stem: Maribel, 14, figure skates at a club in the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic movement. Near the end of a meeting at the rink she says that an assistant coach has been touching her under her costume after evening practices, most recently last week. She and the consultant are in view of the front desk, the coach is away at a competition until Sunday, and her mother is due to collect her in ten minutes. She asks, "What happens now?" Once she has been listened to and is with her mother, what should the consultant do?
options: Report to child protective services or police, and to the U.S. Center for SafeSport
Call emergency services and stay beside her until officers reach the rink
Report to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, which will decide whom else to involve
Give the club's director a written account, as the club's conduct policy asks
rationales: Sexual abuse of a minor must be reported promptly to child protective services or law enforcement, and in the Olympic and Paralympic movement to the U.S. Center for SafeSport as well. The consultant reports what she said and leaves investigating to them.
Calling emergency services first fits a child in immediate danger. She is with her mother and the coach is out of town, so the prompt reports are the next step.

A report to the Center alone can fit misconduct that isn't child abuse or a crime. Suspected child abuse also goes directly to civil authorities, and reporting to one body doesn't replace reporting to the other.
The club's own procedure may be enough for a breach such as lateness or rude conduct. For suspected abuse, telling the club doesn't satisfy the duty to report to the authorities.
takeaway: Suspected child abuse goes promptly to civil authorities and, in Olympic and Paralympic sport, also to SafeSport.

stem: Torvald, a professional cellist, stays seated when his session ends. He says he has been thinking about dying for months. Asked directly, he says that he has been saving up his sleeping pills, that they are in the bag at his feet, and that he means to take them when he gets home tonight. He lives alone and has an appointment with his therapist on Thursday, two days away. The consultant isn't a licensed clinician. He thanks her for asking and reaches for his coat. What should the consultant do?
options: Ask his consent to let his therapist know before Thursday what he has said
Ask him to wait while she contacts emergency services, and stay with him
Help him find a clinician who can see him within the next few days
Ask him whether he has thought about how he would do it, and when
rationales: Coordinating with his therapist, with consent, fits distress without immediate danger. A plan for tonight with the means at hand can't wait for consent or for Thursday.

A stated intent, a plan for tonight, and the means within reach are imminent risk. The consultant follows the emergency plan, stays with him, and brings in emergency help; protecting life is a limit of confidentiality.
Connecting him with a clinician soon fits serious distress without a plan or intent. He has both, and may act in hours.
Asking directly about a plan and timing is the right step when someone mentions thoughts of dying. He has already answered those questions.
takeaway: Intent, a plan, and access to means is an emergency: stay with the person and get emergency help now.
